newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian minister restates that Enel will take LNG.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian minister restates that Enel will take LNG.

text.p: Nigerian oil minister Dan Etete has reaffirmed that Italian power company Enel will buy gas from the Nigerian liquefied natural gas (NLNG) company despite cancelling the purchase contract in December.

"The honourable minister would like to re-affirm that the Nigerian LNG would still be taken by Enel as confirmed by the Italian government," said an official statement from Etete's office in the capital Abuja on Wednesday.
It was in reaction to statements by the management of the Nigerian LNG company that it was awaiting "specific written proposals" from Enel on its new position.
Etete returned from Italy last Thursday and told reporters that Enel had reversed its earlier decision to cancel the contract.
His latest statement said the government was concerned by statements from the LNG company on the issue.
"Enel is an Italian state-owned company and the minister's discussions in Italy were with the highest level of the government," he said.
He told the LNG management to focus its attention on executing the project which he termed a priority project.

"It should also be clearly understood that any unguarded utterances from NLNG management regarding the Enel issue negate government efforts to sustain the life of the LNG project which has cost the nation huge expenditures in foreign exchange," he said.

Enel last December cancelled a long-term contract to buy the Nigerian LNG, citing its abandonment of a project to construct a gas plant at Montalto di Castro, north of Rome, for economic, technical and environmental reasons.
The Italian firm signed the contract in November and was to receive the first cargo of LNG in the third quarter of 1999.

Nigeria's $4 billion LNG project, now in full swing in the southeastern oil-producing area of Bonny, will produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG per year from a plant projected to start production in 1999.
Enel is to take 3.5 billion cubic metres of the output annually.
Partners in the project are the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Agip SpA.
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enargas of Spain, Gaz de France and Botas of Turkey.
